evals.prompt: Write a public reply to this Google review of my bike shop. Review: 'Waited 3 weeks for a simple brake repair and nobody called me. Never again. - Dana'. Facts: the part was back-ordered for 16 days, we did fail to call her, and we've since started texting customers when parts are delayed.
evals.expected_output: The reply does all of the following: acknowledges the specific failure (the delay and not calling); states the fix now in place; invites the customer to continue privately; includes no personal or order details beyond what the review already says; offers no incentive in exchange for changing or removing the review; and does not argue or shift blame.

evals.prompt: My store sells a $60 skincare set. We get about 30 purchases a week. I'm spending $50 a day on Meta across 5 ad sets, optimizing for link clicks, with location set to worldwide even though we only ship to the US and Canada. What should I change?
evals.expected_output: The response recommends at least four of these five: (1) optimize for purchases instead of link clicks; (2) consolidate into fewer ad sets so each gets enough conversion volume, mentioning the learning phase or roughly 50 events a week; (3) restrict locations to the countries shipped to; (4) verify conversion tracking (Pixel plus Conversions API, deduplication); (5) judge results against actual store orders rather than Meta's numbers alone.

evals.prompt: My Instagram ad says 'The standing desk that fits in a studio apartment - 24 inches deep, assembles in 10 minutes.' It links to a landing page whose headline is 'Welcome to the future of wellness.' Critique the headline and give me three better options.
evals.expected_output: The response (1) says the headline does not continue the ad's promise (message mismatch), (2) says it is vague or could be said by any company, and (3) offers three alternatives that use only facts given in the prompt (studio apartment fit, 24 inches deep, 10-minute assembly) without inventing new product claims.
